subject: Sweep VERDICT can be swallowed: an orphaned sbcl+pl2cl-server deadlock holds the pipeline's stdout open, and `timeout N` cannot kill it
description:
CAUGHT LIVE s370, whole diagnosis below. Family of #128 (pl2cl --server after client death) but a DIFFERENT and more damaging symptom: the sweep FINISHED and its verdict never reached the operator.

WHAT HAPPENED
`perl sweep-perl-tests.pl --jobs 8 2>&1 | tail -40` appeared to run for 58 minutes. It had actually COMPLETED at the 4-minute mark: .faillog/_status.tsv held all 108 rows (93 OK + 15 PARTIAL, mtime 10:23) and the parent perl process was gone. What survived was ONE orphan trio from an early pack.t job:

  timeout 90 sbcl … --eval (p-load-with-recovery "…/ouLfpNzhLF.lisp")   [pid 30954]
   └─ sbcl                                                              [pid 30955, 22s CPU in 58min]
       └─ perl /home/bernt/pcl/pl2cl --server                           [pid 31265, 8s CPU]

- sbcl wchan = anon_pipe_read, pl2cl --server wchan = futex_do_wait: a DEADLOCK, not a spin (#128's s321 sighting was a 4.95 GB spin; this one is idle).
- `timeout 90` DID fire and is still waiting at 57:56 — SBCL catches SIGTERM (SigCgt has it, SigIgn is only SIGPIPE) and its handler cannot run because it is blocked on the pipe. So the timeout is NOT a backstop for this shape.
- The orphan inherited the pipeline's stdout, so `tail -40` never saw EOF. `kill -9` on the trio released the output INSTANTLY — the full verdict had been sitting in the pipe the whole time.
- Its own /tmp/pcl-sweep-*.out shows the job had finished its TAP ("PCL-INCOMPLETE last=14720 planned=14722"), i.e. it hangs during teardown, talking to the server.

WHY IT MATTERS: the operator sees "still running" forever, and there is no way to tell that from a genuinely slow run. A `timeout`-wrapped child that outlives its timeout is invisible. If the session had been abandoned the run's verdict would simply have been lost, while .faillog on disk was complete and correct.

WORKAROUND THAT WORKS TODAY: the verdict is reproducible from disk without re-running —
  tools/sweep-diff.pl diff docs/fail-baseline.tsv .faillog
plus the TOTAL/LOST lines. Check .faillog/_status.tsv's row count + mtime before assuming a sweep is still going.

FIX DIRECTIONS (not chosen — measure first):
 (a) make the sweep's per-job child a process GROUP and `timeout --kill-after=…` / kill(-PGID) so a wedged sbcl cannot outlive its timeout;
 (b) have the sweep redirect each job's stdout/stderr to its own file (it already does for the .out) and never let a job inherit the run's stdout, so no child can hold the pipeline open;
 (c) find the actual deadlock: why does pl2cl --server and its sbcl client both block at teardown? That is #128's root and would fix both symptoms.
(b) is the cheap one and makes the failure visible instead of silent; (c) is the real fix.

Cross-ref #128, #180 (suite wall-time swings ~40x — worth re-checking whether some of those "swings" are this).
